state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Interesting perspective. Let's explore this further. Can you think of any examples where changing all values by the same proportion does affect the range?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Hmm, I'm not really sure... like, if we cut all the plants in half, wouldn't the range get smaller because all the numbers are getting smaller? But I thought that meant it wouldn't change... I'm confused about what "proportion" means and how it's different from just adding the same number to everything.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: That's a great observation! Let's think about why changing all values by the same proportion might affect the range differently than just adding the same number to everything.
